key_insight: CMC-Seg combined CNN and Mamba features with cross-attention, achieving the highest reported mean Dice (81.20%) and lowest inference GFLOPs (381.49) among tested models.
clinical_relevance: Automated segmentation could support glioma assessment before and after treatment, including resection cavities, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: A coarse segmentation model extracted tumor-centered patches from multiparametric MRI.
CMC-Seg used cross-attention-guided Mamba and CNN features for fine-grained segmentation.
Ablation studies assessed multi-direction scanning and cross-attention.
evidence_signal: On the BraTS 2025 test set, CMC-Seg achieved 77.09% non-enhancing tumor core Dice, 78.63% resection cavity Dice, and 4.39 mm HD95; performance was comparable to CNN/Mamba baselines and significantly better than Transformer baselines (P < 0.05).
watch_item: The abstract does not report external clinical validation, so generalizability beyond the benchmark remains uncertain.
paper_title: A Cascaded Framework with a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN Model for Pre- and Post-Treatment Glioma Segmentation
